details:
AstroVitals: Astronaut Health Monitoring System

1. Purpose

AstroVitals is a local web dashboard that tracks the health of astronauts during a mission. It records their vital parameters, compares them to reference values and personal baselines, raises alerts when something is out of range, gives basic advice, and uses Python to analyze trends and predict problems before they become serious.

2. Users

  • Astronaut: logs in to their own account, enters or views their data, and sees alerts and advice.
  • Flight surgeon / crew supervisor (optional): sees all astronauts and their alerts.

3. Monitored parameters

Each parameter has a unit, a normal range, a warning range, and a critical range. All of these are configurable.

Group

Parameters

Cardiovascular

Heart rate, blood pressure (systolic/diastolic)

Respiratory

Respiratory rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂)

Thermal

Body temperature

Body

Weight, hydration status

Sleep and fatigue

Sleep duration and quality, fatigue level

Environment

Cabin CO₂, cabin pressure, radiation dose

Musculoskeletal

Exercise time per day, bone and muscle indicators (long-term)

Mental

Stress or mood self-report

The final list and the "changes observed in flight" should come from your astronaut_parameter_changes.xlsx, so the thresholds are based on real spaceflight data and not Earth-only values.

4. Functional modules

  1. Authentication. Create an account and log in per astronaut, with each astronaut seeing only their own data.
  2. Data entry. Manual forms for now. Later, live sensor input, plus an optional automatic data generator for demos and testing.
  3. Deviations and advice. Each value is compared to the normal range and to the astronaut's own baseline. The module shows the deviation and a short recommendation, for example rest, hydrate, retest, or contact the doctor.
  4. History and charts. A time series per parameter, with normal bands shown on the graph and filters by date and parameter.
  5. Unusual events. The astronaut describes a symptom. The system then asks for the relevant parameters for that symptom and records the event with its context.
  6. Alerts. Triggered when a parameter is too high or too low. There are three levels: normal, warning, critical, with a visible notification on the dashboard.
  7. Predictive analysis (Python). Trend detection, anomaly detection, and short-term forecasts.

5. Alert logic

  • A parameter is compared to fixed thresholds and to the astronaut's personal baseline.
  • Level: normal, warning, critical.
  • A rate-of-change check catches fast drifts even when values are still inside the range.
  • Combined rules can flag multi-parameter patterns, for example high heart rate with low SpO₂ and high temperature.

6. Architecture

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, React (dashboard, forms, charts).
  • Backend: Python (analysis, alert rules, predictions), exposed to the frontend through a local API.
  • Storage: a local database holding users, measurements, events, alerts, and thresholds.
  • Data flow: entry or sensor → validation → storage → rule check and alert → display, with the Python analysis running on the stored history.
